Operations Manual
:::

## Purpose

Use the reporting routes to turn approved public metric releases or a finished
bespoke analysis into a controlled public report.

## Choose the report route

| Product | Preparation | Approval | Publication |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Rolling three-month CVD update** | One controlled builder verifies and freezes exact approved event and mortality release CSVs. | No second analytical approval: the inputs have already been approved and the template may perform only authorised simple display arithmetic. | The builder writes the dated report package; Quarto rendering and GitHub deployment remain separate. |
| **Annual CVD report** | Step 1 builds the private annual PDF and its final one-page public-health-update appendix, extracts the update as a standalone PDF, and prepares both landing pages and shared metadata. | Step 2 records one approval for the exact five-file annual-report and update payload. | Step 3 publishes only that approved payload. |
| **One-off CVD report** | The bespoke analysis is completed first. Step 1 prepares the finished PDF as a private candidate. | Step 2 records approval of the exact candidate. | Step 3 publishes only the approved payload. |

## Responsibilities

- The **BNR Analyst** confirms sources, methods, results, interpretation and
  disclosure safety.
- The **BNR Lead**, **BNR Analyst** or **BNR Developer**, where authorised,
  records approval for annual and one-off candidates.
- The authorised publisher runs the separate publication step and confirms
  that it promoted the approved payload only.
- The **BNR Developer** maintains the shared reporting controls and the Quarto
  presentation without moving analytical calculation into the website layer.

One person may perform more than one action where BNR governance permits, but
the actions and their evidence remain separate.

## Evidence retained

For a rolling update, retain the report identity, build metadata and complete
frozen copies of both source releases. For annual and one-off reports, retain
the private candidate, public manifest, `approval.yml`, publication log and
authoritative published products. The annual candidate includes both the full
report and its standalone one-page update. Private review evidence remains
outside Git.

## Stop points

Stop if a source release is not approved, a package identity changes, a
required value is unavailable or protected, disclosure review is incomplete,
or the approved payload differs from the payload proposed for publication.
Correct the source or version-controlled code and rerun; never correct a
generated report manually.
